programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[2.2, 1.45, 0.28])
mass court = courtyard(base, margin_ratio=0.18, open_side="west")
mass lifted = lift(court, rise_ratio=0.22, support_ratio=0.18)
mass result = carve_void(lifted, margin_ratio=0.12, open_side="west")
programs.name: result_01
programs.rationale: Single calm slab with a public court and lifted base. The operator tree is shallow but spatially clear: ground void, public threshold, then light upper plate.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[2.8, 0.62, 0.48])
mass stepped = stepped_mass(base, direction="x", levels=4, setback_ratio=0.14, shift_per_level=[0.10, 0.00, 0.00])
mass result = cut_corner(stepped, corner="nw", distance=0.16, ratio=0.22)
programs.name: result_02
programs.rationale: Long bar transformed into a stepped section, then clipped at one corner to sharpen entry and frontage. Distinct from courtyard schemes by emphasizing sectional progression and linear urban edge.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[1.35, 1.35, 1.05])
mass mass1 = bend(base, axis="y", angle_degrees=24, subdivisions=4)
mass result = carve_void(mass1, margin_ratio=0.16, open_side="west")
programs.name: result_03
programs.rationale: Compact block is bent to create a continuous curved body, then opened into a usable void. This produces a different topology from stepped or split masses while keeping a legible central figure.

programs.dsl:
mass profile = extruded_polygon(points=[[0.00, 0.00], [1.00, 0.00], [1.18, 0.42], [0.62, 0.92], [0.00, 0.72]], holes=[], height=1.00, divisions=1)
mass hall = profiled_hall(profiled_hall(profile, section_family="ridge", section_controls=[[0.00, 0.82], [0.50, 1.00], [1.00, 0.76]], span_axis="x"), section_family="shed", section_controls=[[0.00, 0.72], [0.55, 1.00], [1.00, 0.80]], span_axis="y")
mass result = clip_fraction(hall, axis="z", fraction=0.82, anchor="start")
programs.name: result_04
programs.rationale: Uses the profiled prism seed explicitly and builds a hall-like mass with controlled roof profile. The topology is hall-first rather than block-first, giving a distinct programmatic and spatial reading.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[0.68, 0.68, 2.5])
mass tower = tapered_tower(base, axis="z", start_scale=[1.00, 1.00], end_scale=[0.56, 0.56], subdivisions=5, scale_top=true)
mass result = slice(tower, normal=[0.00, 1.00, 0.00], offset_ratio=0.18, keep_side="front")
programs.name: result_05
programs.rationale: Vertical tower seed is tightened into a tapered stack and then sliced to open one face. The result reads as a compact urban marker with a controlled public edge and upper hierarchy.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[2.2, 1.45, 0.28])
mass wings = split_wing(base, axis="x", gap_ratio=0.24, bridge=true, height_ratio=0.72, ground_spine=true, ground_spine_height_ratio=0.18, ground_spine_width_ratio=0.16)
mass result = bridge(wings, wings, width=0.20, height=0.22, height_ratio=0.54, z=0.32)
programs.name: result_06
programs.rationale: A slab is split into two wings with a public gap, then reconnected by a bridge. This creates a two-part figure with a central passage, materially different from single-mass carvings.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[1.60, 1.20, 0.95])
mass core = courtyard(base, margin_ratio=0.22, open_side="west")
mass over = cantilever(core, start_ratio=0.58, vector=[0.18, 0.00, 0.00])
mass result = union(over, core)
programs.name: result_07
programs.rationale: Compact block becomes a courtyard ring with a modest cantilevered upper shift. The topology is ring-plus-overhang, reinforcing public ground use without becoming too fragmented.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[2.8, 0.62, 0.48])
mass curved = bent_bar(base, axis="y", angle_degrees=18, subdivisions=4)
mass pierced = puncture(curved, axis="z", count=3, ratio=0.12, n=3)
mass result = lift(pierced, rise_ratio=0.16, support_ratio=0.14)
programs.name: result_08
programs.rationale: An active bar is gently bent, punctured, and lifted to create a porous street-building condition. The spatial idea is linear yet filtered, unlike the more solid courtyard or stepped variants.
